text: noted an in- creased risk when the carbamazepine component of the regimen was withdrawn.86 It should be borne in mind that withdrawal of an enzyme-inducing antiepileptic may alter the serum concentrations of other drugs in the regimen87 • there is also controversy about the prognostic value of the EEG for the success of withdrawal.75-77,83 Although an abnormal EEG before withdrawal was a negative prognostic factor in many studies, EEG abnormalities are not present in all epileptic patients, and some antie- pileptic drugs suppress EEG abnormalities and can lead to false-negative results75 When a decision to withdraw is made, it is agreed that the withdrawal regimen should be gradual to reduce the risk of provoking withdrawal seizures. Drugs should be with- drawn one at a time but there is no agreement on the order or the optimum rate of withdrawal for individual drugs. It has been suggested that tapering therapy over less than 6 months increases the relapse rate.75 However, one study in children indicated no significant difference in seizure re- currence rate when various antiepileptics, including bar- biturates, were withdrawn over 6 weeks or 9 months.88 Nonetheless, it has been pointed out that relapses tended to occur earlier in the group tapered more rapidly, and in practice it is rarely necessary to withdraw medication more rapidly than over a 6-month period.75 It may be possible to Antiepileptics 467 The symbol † denotes a preparation no longer actively marketed The symbol  denotes a substance whose use may be restricted in certain sports (see p.vii) withdraw phenytoin or valproate quickly (over a few days in hospital) if necessary. If seizures recur on withdrawal it is almost always possible to restore good control by re-instituting therapy, and mor- bidity, mortality, and incidence of status epilepticus are re- ported to be low in the setting of prescribed antiepileptic drug withdrawal.75 However, in a very small number of patients intractable seizures may develop.89 1.
